subject: smelt
title: 17 oracled fuzz targets with committed regression seeds replayed in CI
one_why: Breaks the anchors' verification-8 ceiling (codex/cline/pi all lack CI fuzzing): smelt_loop fuzzes the whole TUI event loop, cache_invariance byte-diffs cached prompt prefixes, store_state replays a persistence state machine, and every fuzz-found bug lands as a seed under fuzz/seeds/<target>/regression/ that `cargo xtask fuzz verify` replays on each PR; fixed-clock/stubbed-I/O determinism makes any crash replayable.

subject: smelt
title: Shell-grammar walker infers tool effects instead of regex deny-listing
one_why: eval_program/and_or/pipeline/if/loop plus heredoc and embedded-command analysis yields ShellRisk and path effects per command with unknown constructs escalated rather than defaulted allow, and the whole evaluator is fuzzed with a workspace-downgrade oracle -- the strongest policy engine found outside codex's execpolicy DSL, and it is rules+effects instead of prompts.

subject: smelt
title: Compaction is entirely a bundled Lua plugin against two engine contracts
one_why: The engine knows only on_prepare_request and RecoverFromContextLimit; the plugin implements triggering (provider-anchored estimate), group-boundary summarization, checkpoint install, cancellation guards, and a failure circuit breaker (compact.lua:94), so compaction tiering is user-replaceable policy rather than baked loop logic -- deeper extension ownership than pi, which keeps compaction in core.

subject: smelt
title: Cache-prefix stability treated as a fuzzed invariant, not a convention
one_why: Canonical sorted tool list, Anthropic <=4 cache_control markers with 5m/1h TTL, session-scoped prompt_cache_key, and two fuzz targets that assert history actions leave the cached prefix byte-identical -- the failure mode (field order or registration drift silently burning tokens) is defended by the fuzzer, not by code review discipline.

subject: smelt
title: Duplicate tool outputs replaced by pointers placed only on the new invocation
one_why: Repeated identical tool results (>=500 bytes) collapse to a short pointer to the prior call id, but the pointer is written on the fresh invocation so already-cached history bytes never mutate -- gets context savings without ever invalidating the provider prompt cache, which naive dedup-on-history would.

subject: smelt
title: Secrets scrubbed from user input and tool results before entering history
one_why: Four-layer detection (provider token prefixes, PEM/JWT/conn-string structure, keyword proximity, Shannon entropy) replaces secrets with labeled [REDACTED:x] placeholders at ingress only -- assistant output is never touched, so model-visible conversation stays truthful while pasted credentials stop reaching providers; pattern source is gitleaks, MIT-compatible.

subject: smelt
title: Sessions live in a content-addressed SQLite lineage store with operator tools
one_why: rusqlite savepoint transactions, sha256 object store, turn state machine with startup-recovery receipts, and first-class `smelt session doctor|backup|gc|vacuum` plus JSONL export -- session durability is engineered like an embedded database with reachability-based reclamation rather than JSONL append-and-hope.

subject: smelt
title: Whole agent surface scriptable in Lua, generated and drift-gated
one_why: Keymaps, commands, autocmds, custom tools, custom permission modes, widgets, and even compaction and plan mode are Lua; the 90-page API reference and type stubs are generated by xtask and CI fails on drift -- the Neovim customization model applied to a coding agent, with the doc-sync gate most projects never build.

subject: smelt
title: Trust model states plainly that nothing below approvals is a boundary
one_why: Same honesty register as pi's SECURITY.md: Lua/plugins/MCP run in-process unsandboxed, approved bash runs with user privileges, and users are told to containerize for untrusted prompts -- no marketing drift between README and enforcement reality.

subject: smelt
title: Goal-gated auto-continue with quota backoff and work guards
one_why: Continuation fires only when the prior turn left concrete in-scope work (default policy), honors an idle gate, retries quota errors on 60s->300s backoff, and every async completion checks a work guard so stale continuations cannot mutate a moved-on session -- a disciplined version of the auto-continue pattern seen elsewhere.
